summary: Gallatin NF lookout near Livingston: observation tower and cabin from 1919, a cabin by 1931, labelled abandoned; listed Gone; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: Observation tower with a cabin (1919 entry); a cabin on the south slope, an eighth of a mile below the summit, by 1931
facts.status_note: The Forest Fire Lookout Association lists it as Gone; firelookout.com labels it Abandoned without using the word gone; no source describes what remains

events.note: Cabin on the south slope, an eighth of a mile below the summit (firelookout.com 1931 entry)

evidence.supports: 1931 cabin on the south slope, 1/8 mile below the summit, labelled abandoned
evidence.quote: 1931: cabin on south slope 1/8 mile below summit. Abandoned.

evidence.supports: about 14 miles northwest of Livingston, Park County, in the Gallatin National Forest
land-survey location 1S-8E-6 under Park County and the Gallatin National Forest
the Forest Fire Lookout Association lists the site as a tower marked Gone, with no register number
evidence.quote: Bangtail Ranger Station Park 45.78436 -110.78197 Tower Gone

notes_for_editor: Thin record: one detailed entry (firelookout.com, a few lines) and the FFLA list row. The Forest Lookouts page for Bangtail (montanalookouts.weebly.com/bangtail-rs.html) is a location stub with no history; it is cited only for the 1S-8E-6 land-survey location. Two web searches found no staffing history, no post-1931 history and no description of the site today. The record's kind 'tower' matches only the 1919 entry; the 1931 cabin is on the slope, so the kind is kept as is rather than corrected. Elevation (7,700 ft) is in the story but not set as a fact, since no field for it is in the facts list; the record's elevation_m is null and can take 2347 m if the editor wants it. No photo found.
